summary: A fiction excerpt from Book 2 in which the narrator talks with Checker by phone after a kidnapping and break-in at his home. Checker reveals he staged his own disappearance to draw off rival groups, and that he cracked a flash drive full of numbers. Arthur appears to have been influenced by Dawna, and the narrator worries about his lasting condition.
one_line: Checker explains he staged his own kidnapping to mislead rival groups, and the narrator discusses Arthur's possible mind control and a numbers-filled flash drive.
key_facts: Checker says he staged the appearance of his own kidnapping so that whichever group arrived first would think the other had beaten him.
Checker says he proxied into his home security system to check that he had escaped safely.
Checker says the Hole was mostly his work, and that the intruders scavenged everything left after they arrived.
The narrator believes the intruders were probably looking for the flash drive, because everyone knows Checker now has it.
Arthur left Checker about seven messages about the flash drive, according to Checker.
Dawna tried to convince Arthur that the flash drive was meaningless, according to the narrator.
The narrator says Pithica is still trying to recover the flash drive, based on a source.
Checker says he cracked the flash drive a few days earlier and that it is mostly numbers.
Checker describes the flash drive contents as lists of numbers totaling gigabytes, and says he has not found a pattern yet.
The narrator says Dawna programmed Arthur, and that Arthur seems to be influenced only regarding this case.
The narrator advises not to trust anything Arthur says about Pithica and to keep Pithica away from him.
The narrator cannot promise Arthur will return to normal, saying there is a good chance but that Dawna may have permanently twisted his mind.
The narrator says she is good at numbers and offers to help with the flash drive.
